$comment: The closed register of representability losses the spec-bundle extraction frontend declares (FR-093 "Declared losses"). Every DECLARED_LOSS diagnostic names exactly one `code` of this register; a loss with no row fails the crate's own test (FR-093-CON-3). The two #78 rows are the frontend's reading of an unruled issue: a ruling that gives the IR an any-type or a presence independent of multiplicity.lower removes them, the JsonObject record, the presence derivation and every golden carrying them in one commit.

losses.construct: a `JsonObject` Type cell: an unconstrained JSON value
losses.lowering: one package-local `record` named `JsonObject` at `ix://<org>/<name>/type/JsonObject` with `fields: []` and `unknownPolicy: preserve`, as packages/semantic-core/kernel-scalars.json prescribes; any JSON value is narrowed to any JSON object

losses.construct: a `0..*` (or `*`) collection field: the source cannot say whether the member must be present and may be empty, and the IR derives `presence` from `multiplicity.lower`
losses.lowering: `presence: optional`; the IR identifies an absent collection with an empty one, so a required-but-possibly-empty collection is emitted as optional

losses.construct: an extraction whose `availability.fields.lossy` is `true`: the engine did not interpret every entry it read (an unresolved placeholder, or a module declaring `compatibility_posture: declared-lossy`)
losses.lowering: the record is lowered from the declarations the engine returned; what the engine did not interpret reaches no IR node
